note: The closest match to the stated ICP in this batch and one of the closest in the corpus. He is a senior transformation executive who runs large technology organisations, currently between roles after a three-year non-compete, advising a private equity firm on an acquisition — 'already successful, business owner or equivalent' is satisfied without argument. Income is confirmed by his own words: 'Financially, I don't need to think... committing to something is not the issue. Funding is fine.' Health is precisely the neglected domain — he built himself intellectually for thirty years and said so at length — and he is not deconditioned: he walks with a weighted vest, rides a Peloton, played soccer and cricket, lifted in his 40s, and his biomarker panel came back broadly clear with a biological age six years below chronological. Good-to-great is the only arguable one, since he described himself as having 'let myself go' and is 25 lb over his historical weight, which is rescue language. But the ICP's own source quote — 'they're still good, but they're kind of wanting to go from good to great', with health as the neglected piece of an otherwise successful life — describes this man almost exactly, so it is scored as a match. The finding that matters is the outcome: the one true-ICP prospect in the batch did not buy, deferred to a written comparison against a local in-person trainer, and every prospect who did commit money in these twelve files sits outside the ICP on income.
